title: Raise a clean error on a malformed config numeric field
lead:
`Config.load` catches only `(KeyError, TypeError)`, but `Config.from_dict` and
`SyncTarget.from_dict` call `int(...)` on `version`, `id.width`, and sync
`count`. A hand-edited or merge-mangled config such as `{"id":{"width":"wide"}}`
raises `ValueError`, which escapes to the top and prints a raw traceback —
violating the "clean SlicerError, never a traceback" invariant. The index/slice
path already catches `ValueError`; only config is exposed.
boundary:
**Not in this slice:** validating semantic ranges of config values beyond "is a
number"; only the crash is in scope.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Broken JSON from a bad merge or hand edit is exactly the case the tool otherwise
handles gracefully. A traceback here is an embarrassing crash and breaks the
`SlicerError.code` contract agents rely on.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Add `ValueError` to the `except` tuple in `Config.load` so it raises the same
`ConfigError`/`code="config"` the non-JSON case already produces. Confirm the
message still names the config file.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
A wrong-typed numeric config field yields a clean, actionable error and exit
code, not a stack trace.
